title: The single-base representation conjecture for sums of exponential terms
statement:
Let $a_n,c_n,b,d\rtin\mathbb{R}$ be real numbers, with $n\in\mathbb{N}$. The expression $a_nb^n+c_nd^n$ is considered as a sum of two terms with possibly different bases.

**Single-base representation conjecture.** For every $a_n,b,c_n,d\in\mathbb{R}$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$, there exist $u_n,{\Greekmath 010D}\in\mathbb{R}$ such that

$$
a_nb^n+c_nd^n=u_n{\Greekmath 010D}^n,
$$

for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$.

This conjecture is proposed as a structural statement intended to help describe the space of finite Taylor measures, whose terms have the form $a_n{\Greekmath 010D}^n/n!$. Its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.04760

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2025).
source_name: Athanasios Christou Micheas, “The Taylor Measure and its Applications”, arXiv:2508.04760 (2025).
